newsitem.title: USA: NASA ends participation in primate space mission.
newsitem.headline: NASA ends participation in primate space mission.

text.p: The U.S. space agency said on Tuesday it will not participate in primate research on next year's Bion 12 mission, calling the risks to rhesus monkeys "unacceptable."
The National Aeronautics and Space Administration said it decided to suspend participation after a rhesus monkey died following the successful flight and landing of the Bion 11 satellite in January.

The monkey, one of two that flew on the two-week international mission launched from Russia, died of a heart attack after post-flight tests. A Russian official said at the time that the death was "an unfortunate incident which couldn't have been foreseen."
NASA said the monkeys faced "unexpected mortality risk associated with anaesthesia for surgical procedures (biopsy of bone and muscle) on the day following return from space."
"NASA has determined that this risk is unacceptable and is therefore discontinuing its participation in the primate experiments on Bion 12."
The Bion programme, a joint project of the U.S., Russian and Franch space agencies, aimed to study the physiological effect of low gravity and space radiation using Russian-owned rhesus monkeys.
U.S. animal rights groups have protested against the mission.
